title: Flattening a finite-type algebraic space by an admissible blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. An effective Cartier divisor is a closed subspace whose ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor. For a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$, a morphism $g:Y\to T$, and $p:T^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$, the strict transform of $Y$ means the closed subspace of $Y\times_TT^{\prime}$ cut out by the ideal of sections locally annihilated by some power of a local equation of the exceptional effective Cartier divisor $p^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$. Let $g:Y\to T$ be of finite type and quasi-separated, meaning that its relative diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Suppose $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $U\subseteq T$ is a quasi-compact open subspace, and $Y\times_TU\to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Then there exists a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal K|_U=\mathcal O_U$ such that the strict transform of $Y$ under $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$ is flat and of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$. Finite presentation here means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated. No Noetherian hypothesis and no finite-presentation hypothesis on $g$ outside $U$ are imposed.

proof.text: First $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For quasi-compactness choose a surjective etale quasi-compact scheme atlas $A\to T$, as permitted by the definition of a quasi-compact space. The affine-test criterion extends the quasi-compactness of $g$ to this quasi-compact scheme test, so $Y_A$ is quasi-compact. Choose a quasi-compact scheme atlas $V\to Y_A$ and compose it with $Y_A\to Y$; this is a surjective etale atlas with quasi-compact source. Composition of quasi-separated morphisms applied to $Y\to T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ gives absolute quasi-separatedness of $Y$. Regard the spaces as spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Apply the existing finite-type envelope theorem to obtain a closed immersion $i:Y\hookrightarrow Z$ and $h:Z\to T$ of finite presentation with $hi=g$. This uses its full qcqs finite-type form, so a separatedness assumption on $g$ is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0872 (lemma-finite-type-closed-in-finite-presentation); Tag 087E proof envelope step, using 0872 directly instead of its separated refinement 0873

proof.text: Put $F=i_*\mathcal O_Y$. Closed-immersion pushforward makes $F$ quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal O_Z\twoheadrightarrow F$ makes it of finite type, locally generated by the image of $1$. On $U$, the map $i_U:Y_U\to Z_U$ is locally of finite presentation: $Y_U\to U$ is so by hypothesis, and $Z_U\to U$ is locally of finite type since $h$ is locally of finite presentation. Base change of the latter assertion is checked on scheme charts by tensor base change of finitely presented algebras. Apply relative finite-presentation permanence to $i_U$, then the closed-structure-module criterion to obtain finite presentation of $(i_U)_*\mathcal O_{Y_U}=F|_{Z_U}$. The equality is the etale module restriction comparison applied to the open immersion $U\to T$.

source.place: Tag 087E (lemma-flat-after-blowing-up), final paragraph: hypotheses on i_* O_Y; Tag 05WT (lemma-finite-presentation-permanence), Tag 084Q (lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation)

proof.text: The module $F|_{Z_U}$ is flat over $U$. To check the precise relative-flatness predicate, take any etale scheme chart $A\to U$. The etale restriction comparison identifies its restriction with the pushforward of $\mathcal O_{Y_A}$ along the closed immersion $Y_A\hookrightarrow Z_A$. The assumed flatness of $Y_U\to U$ implies flatness of $Y_A\to A$ on its scheme charts. The closed-pushforward relative-flatness theorem applies with scheme base $A$ and gives flatness of that pushforward over $A$. This proves the required condition for every $A$, without applying the scheme-base theorem directly to the possibly nonschematic space $U$.

source.place: Tag 087E proof: flatness of i_* O_Y over U; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0DK1 (lemma-stalk-push-closed), with the usual image-point subscripts

proof.text: The space $Z$ is quasi-compact: use a quasi-compact scheme atlas $A\to T$, quasi-compactness of $h$ to get quasi-compact $Z_A$, and compose a quasi-compact scheme atlas of $Z_A$ with $Z_A\to Z$, exactly as for $Y$ in step 1. Apply module flattening to $(h:Z\to T,F,U)$. Here $h$ is locally of finite presentation, $T$ is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact, $F$ is finite type, and steps 2 and 3 give both conditions on $F|_{Z_U}$. Obtain a finite-type ideal $\mathcal K$ equal to $\mathcal O_U$ over $U$, with blowup $T'\to T$, such that the module strict transform $F'$ is of finite presentation and flat over $T'$.

Let $Y'$ be the strict transform. Choose an etale scheme atlas $A\to T$ and an etale scheme atlas $W\to Z_A$. Put $D=Y\times_Z W$, a scheme closed in $W$, and $A'=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K\mathcal O_A}A$. Etale localization of transforms identifies $A'$ with $T'\times_T A$, and identifies the restrictions of $Y'$ and $F'$ on $W\times_A A'$ with the space and module strict transforms of $D$ and $(D\hookrightarrow W)_*\mathcal O_D$. These torsion transforms are the scheme transforms used below: on a scheme, a local section of a quasi-coherent module vanishes off the locally principal exceptional divisor $V(t)$ exactly when, on affine opens, a power of $t$ kills it, since the supported-section kernel is the kernel of restriction to the complement. So the module transform is that of the scheme definition, and the structure-sheaf clause of the strict-transform kernel lemma identifies $D'$, cut out by the torsion ideal, with the scheme strict transform $D^b$ of the transfer theorem. The input module identity is the etale pushforward restriction comparison. Now apply the existing scheme closed-immersion transfer theorem to $D\hookrightarrow W\to A$: $W\to A$ is locally of finite presentation, since it is etale over the base change of $h$. It identifies the transformed module with the pushforward structure module of the transformed closed scheme, and its final implication gives flatness and local finite presentation of that scheme over $A'$. The module hypotheses hold because they are the restrictions of those on $F'$. These transformed charts cover $Y'$ and $T'$; the scheme-chart criterion therefore proves $Y'\to T'$ flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 087E concluding paragraph, reduced by spaces-divisors.tex Tag 0863 (lemma-strict-transform-local) to flat.tex Tag 081R final paragraph, as packaged in the scheme transfer node

proof.text: Finally $Y'\hookrightarrow Y\times_TT'$ is closed by its definition. A closed immersion is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests: over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ its source is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, which is quasi-compact. It is separated (its diagonal is an isomorphism), hence quasi-separated. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $Y\times_TT'\to T'$ follow by base change from $g$, and their composition with the closed immersion has both properties. For quasi-compactness on all tests use the affine-test criterion; composition on quasi-compact tests is simply the iterated fibre-product identity. With step 5 this is finite presentation in exactly the convention of the statement. The ideal supplied in step 4 is $U$-admissible, so this completes all the asserted clauses.
